sources.title: Giovanni Antonio Cavazzi da Montecuccolo, Istorica Descrizione de' tre regni Congo, Matamba et Angola (1687) — Capuchin missionary's detailed firsthand account of time spent at her court
Portuguese colonial correspondence and administrative records, Arquivo Histórico Ultramarino — an independent, frequently adversarial source given her recurring conflict with Portugal
Dutch West India Company (WIC) trading and military records from the 1641-1648 alliance period — a third, independent European source tradition
Linda M. Heywood, Njinga of Angola: Africa's Warrior Queen (2017) — scholarly biography drawing on all three source traditions

social_assertiveness.rationale: At a 1622 diplomatic meeting, the Portuguese governor offered her no seat as a calculated insult; she had one of her own attendants kneel to serve as her seat, meeting him eye-to-eye — a specific episode documented by Cavazzi and corroborated in substance by Portuguese colonial records.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Personally led troops in battle at multiple documented points across four decades of armed resistance against Portuguese colonial forces, not a single campaign.

adaptability.rationale: Shifted from opposing all European powers to a formal military and trade alliance with the Dutch West India Company against Portugal (1641-1648), then adapted her strategy again after the Dutch were expelled in 1648 — two specific, dated geopolitical realignments, not a fixed strategy.

persistence.rationale: Sustained armed and diplomatic resistance to Portuguese colonization for roughly four decades (1620s-1663), through multiple military defeats and displacements, until negotiating a peace treaty near the end of her life on her own terms.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Sustained decades of direct armed conflict with Portuguese colonial forces, documented across Portuguese, Dutch, and missionary source traditions independently.

independent_thinking.rationale: Converted to Christianity for diplomatic purposes during Portuguese negotiations, then documented adapting her religious and political practice again as circumstances shifted — genuine strategic flexibility that is also, honestly, in tension with a claim of fixed principle, scored as dual_edged rather than resolved in one direction.

proactive_agency.rationale: Initiated the alliance with the Dutch herself as a deliberate countermove against Portuguese pressure, rather than accepting Portuguese terms or waiting on events.

planning_orientation.rationale: Sustained a decades-long strategy of shifting alliances between European powers while deliberately absorbing refugees and escaped enslaved people to rebuild her population and military base — a documented, sustained strategic pattern, not a single tactical decision.

leadership_drive.rationale: Ruled as queen of Ndongo from 1624 and Matamba from 1631, personally commanding forces, for nearly four decades until her death — a sustained, documented pattern of holding and exercising authority.

decisiveness.rationale: The 1622 seating episode required immediate, in-the-moment improvisation during a live diplomatic encounter with no time to plan a response in advance.

autonomy_need.rationale: Consistently refused Portuguese demands for vassalage across four decades, even when accepting subordinate status would have been the materially easier path, evidenced by the sustained conflict itself.

achievement_drive.rationale: Sustained pursuit of territorial rule and sovereignty across an unusually long life — she was still actively ruling and negotiating a peace treaty on her own terms at approximately eighty years old.

collaboration.rationale: Sustained a real, multi-year military and trade partnership with the Dutch West India Company (1641-1648), documented independently in Dutch trading and military records.

persuasiveness.rationale: Successfully negotiated both the Dutch alliance and, later, a peace treaty with Portugal near the end of her life, inferred from the documented outcomes of those negotiations.

cross_domain_range.rationale: Functioned across military command, cross-cultural diplomacy with two rival European powers, and internal state administration (population and refugee policy) — three genuinely distinct domains with real documented activity in each.

ambiguity_tolerance.rationale: Sustained rule and resistance through decades of shifting alliances, military reversals, and displacement, evidenced by the continuity of her rule across that whole uncertain period.

impact_motivation.rationale: Sustained a four-decade commitment to resisting colonization and preserving her kingdom's sovereignty rather than accepting an easier, earlier accommodation with Portugal, evidenced by the consistency of that resistance across her whole reign.

discipline.rationale: Sustaining organized resistance and governance across four decades implies real personal and organizational discipline, but no single cited discipline-specific episode survives independent of the broader resistance record, hence inference-level.

provenance.notes: Roster-12 new-intake batch (2026-09): Sub-Saharan Africa / early_modern pick, and a genuinely rare case of three independently-sourced European traditions (Portuguese colonial records, Dutch WIC records, an Italian Capuchin missionary's firsthand account) plus modern archive-based scholarship (Heywood) converging on the same figure rather than a single tradition. The religious-conversion pragmatism is scored honestly as dual_edged (independent_thinking) rather than read only as strategic genius. Scored to completion before any eligibility check was run.
